source.title: Bidirectional Looking with A Novel Double Exponential Moving Average to Adaptive and Non-adaptive Momentum Optimizers
source.authors: Yi-Neng Chen; Z. Li; Le-Fei Zhang; Bo Du; Hai Zhao

record.tranche_reason: Compares held-out performance of adaptive and non-adaptive optimizers using the study's own experiments, with different optimizer variants and tasks from the claim's cited comparisons.
record.gate_note: The paper compares optimizer performance on held-out test or development sets. It does not test random-label memorization, width beyond interpolation, architecture bias, batch-size effects, dropout, sharpness measures, or memorized-example removal. Training-loss values are discussed but are not included as separate rows because they do not measure the held-out-performance comparison in V4.
record.test_reason: The study directly compares Adam with momentum SGD on CIFAR test accuracy under limited learning-rate tuning. Equal training performance is an optional feature of V4, not a prerequisite for testing its held-out-performance claim.
record.authors_conclusion: The authors conclude that their DEMA and dynamic lookahead framework improves optimization across diverse tasks, with AdmetaR and AdmetaS improving their respective RAdam and SGDM baselines in the CIFAR experiments. They describe faster initial convergence for adaptive methods and better final CIFAR performance for the SGD family. Their broad claims of improvement have exceptions, including BERTlarge SQuAD v2.0, where AdmetaR trails RAdam. They acknowledge additional computation and hyperparameters.
record.recipe_differences: Compares several optimizers on standard image-classification and language tasks; introduces and evaluates A DMETA variants. It does not reproduce the cited optimizer-generalization studies' experiments.
record.method_sensitivity: The relative optimizer results vary by dataset, architecture, and model size; on CIFAR-10 and CIFAR-100, the SGD-family versus Adam-family comparison differs between ResNet-110 and PyramidNet. GLUE results also vary between BERTbase and BERTlarge.

fits_no_version.finding: RAdam's GLUE averages exceed AdamW's by 0.08 points for BERTbase and 0.53 points for BERTlarge.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Adaptive optimizer variants can differ in held-out performance when fine-tuning BERT; this comparison does not establish an adaptive-versus-SGD generalization difference.

record.peer_reviewed: International Conference on Machine Learning; Proceedings of the 40th International Conference on Machine Learning, PMLR 202, 2023
record.problems: The comparisons are not reported as matched for training performance across optimizers. The CIFAR experiments use tuned hyperparameters but the paper says baseline settings may differ from their original papers. Some reported GLUE outcomes are averages across datasets, masking task-level differences.
record.rows_left_out: Held-out scores for additional adaptive optimizers, A DMETA variants, SQuAD, NER, and audio tasks were not extracted because the row budget was focused on direct Adam-family versus SGD-family comparisons for V4. These results appear in Tables 1–4 and Table 11; the study does not report the specific comparisons required by V1–V3 or V5–V8.

untested.parts: Convolutional versus fully connected architectures and local connectivity.

Adaptive-versus-SGD comparisons on language benchmarks; systematic broader hyperparameter tuning; decoupled weight decay as a remedy; word-level language modeling. Appendix G reports post-Adam SGDM training, but does not establish recovery relative to continued Adam under a matched additional training budget. Equal or better Adam training performance is not established numerically for the extracted comparisons.

missing.what: ResNet-110 learning-rate sensitivity: changing SGDM's learning rate from 0.1 to 0.5 changes CIFAR-10 accuracy from 93.68% to 93.65% and CIFAR-100 accuracy from 72.07% to 73.48%. Both settings still exceed Adam's respective scores. This additional tuning result is not declared in rows_left_out.

record.verdict_notes: The apparent architecture-dependent reversal in the record results from copying plain SGD scores into the two PyramidNet SGDM rows. GLUE comparisons between adaptive optimizers do not justify a V4 scope limitation. Appendix E fixes baseline momentum parameters and weight decay while searching learning rates; it does not conduct broad tuning.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label fitting and natural-label generalization coexistence.
Width sweeps beyond the interpolation threshold.
Convolutional versus fully connected architecture comparisons.

The paper compares optimizers on several tasks, but does not test all benchmarks named in the version or the effects of broader tuning, decoupled weight decay, or switching from Adam to SGD. It does not report matched training performance for every optimizer comparison.
Large-batch comparisons and batch-size-dependent generalization gaps.
Dropout effects and interactions with augmentation or weight decay.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and its relationship to generalization gaps.
Removing memorized examples and measuring the effect on test accuracy.

relationships.condition: ResNet-110 and PyramidNet trained from scratch on CIFAR-10 and CIFAR-100 for 160 epochs, with fixed weight decay and learning-rate searches
relationships.reason: SGDM exceeds Adam in all four comparisons: 93.68 versus 91.89, 72.07 versus 68.45, 95.08 versus 94.55, and 79.49 versus 76.72 percent; R6 and R8 require correction from SGD to SGDM values (R1–R8).
relationships.display_finding: Reported test accuracies favor momentum SGD over Adam in all four comparisons, but these results remain unverified.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
